precepts.text: He shall have dominion from sea to sea and from the river unto the ends of the earth, and his enemies shall lick the dust.
precepts.point: By the blood of thy covenant, the everlasting covenant of Christ's death, I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water: this is the pit, the valley of dry bones, and no water is no truth.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says the King “shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.” David says the same: “He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.” And he reads on: “They that dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust.”

They are scared of the saying from the river to the sea. Well, that's in the Bible too. And it is not just that little area. It is from sea to sea, meaning the whole planet earth is ours. When we went into the land, the Lord gave us that portion according to the number of the children of Israel, but the whole earth really belongs to us, to the ends of the earth.

In that day “I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off”, meaning we would have no military during that time. The King's dominion is our defence, and his enemies shall lick the dust.

precepts.text: He shall judge the poor, save the children of the needy and break in pieces the oppressor: no coming together with him.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

precepts.text: The poor of His people is the people of Zion, the Israelites, who shall trust in what the Most High has founded.
precepts.point: He shall break in pieces the oppressor, which is why this is pointing to things to come, the Kingdom of Heaven.

note.label: Psalm 72: All Nations Shall Serve Him

precepts.why:
David asks the Most High to give the king his judgments and the king's son his righteousness, so that “He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.” Who is the poor? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people is the people of Zion, the Israelites, who shall trust in what the Most High has founded. So when the king's son judges the poor with judgment and “shall save the children of the needy”, it is the Israelites being judged rightly and saved.

“The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness”, and he “shall break in pieces the oppressor.” That is why this is pointing to things to come, the Kingdom of Heaven, when the poor of Zion are saved and their oppressor is broken.

precepts.text: Israel will remain on this earth as long as the sun, moon, stars, and all the ordinances of heaven are still in place.
precepts.point: He shall have dominion from sea to sea and from the river unto the ends of the earth, meaning he will rule the entire planet.

note.label: Psalm 72: All Nations Shall Serve Him

precepts.why:
“They shall fear thee as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.” The poor of his people will fear the Most High and keep his commandments throughout all generations, as long as the sun and moon endure. Jeremiah shows why the sun and moon are the measure: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.”

Israel will remain on this earth as long as the sun, moon, stars and all the ordinances of heaven are still in place. Only if those ordinances depart would the seed of Israel cease from being a nation, and they have not departed.

So the people who fear him as long as the sun and moon endure are Israel, and the king's son who “shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth” will rule the entire planet over them, with “abundance of peace so long as the moon endureth.”

precepts.text: He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.
precepts.point: I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more.

note.label: Zechariah 9: Thy King Cometh Unto Thee, Just and Having Salvation

precepts.why:
He will encamp about his house, and no oppressor shall pass through them any more. “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.”

The oppressor is broken in pieces, and the poor of the people and the children of the needy are saved; that is why no oppressor passes through his house any more.

precepts.text: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents, and all kings shall fall down before him.
precepts.point: Wise men come from the east to Jerusalem to worship him. This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

precepts.why:
“there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.” This is prophetic; it was written that kings from far off would come and bow before him.

“The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him.” Kings from Tarshish, the isles, Sheba and Seba, far countries, bringing presents, offering gifts and falling down before him. The wise men from the east coming to worship the one born King of the Jews are the beginning of that psalm being fulfilled, and it ends with all kings falling down before him and all nations serving him.
